module: Mesh weight diagnostic during an import (the editor's city/network importer). Distinguishes UNIQUE geometry (ProceduralMesh: buildings, bridge or tunnel decks, gantries, each with its own buffer and its own collision build) from INSTANCED geometry (TSStatics grouped by shape, Forest items). Generators call recordMesh during construction; the importer calls begin() at the start and report() at the end, which logs a summary per family.
usage:
local ms = require('editor/toolUtilities/meshStats')
ms.begin()
ms.recordMesh('bld_12', 'building', nVerts, nTris)
ms.recordParts('bridge.deck', nVerts, nTris)
ms.report('import')
notes: Collection is active only between begin() and report(): outside this window, recordMesh and recordParts have no effect, so normal editing does not touch the counters.

report() re-checks each recorded name in the scene (scenetree.findObject): a mesh renamed or deleted during the import is not counted; it also enumerates all TSStatics (grouped by shapeName file), the Forest's items and the WaterBlock/WaterPlane objects.
The outputs are level I log lines prefixed '[mesh]' (per family: meshes, triangles, vertices; breakdown of merged parts; instanced props; HEADLINE line).

begin.desc: Starts a collection window: enables collection and clears previous records.

recordMesh.desc: Records a ProceduralMesh by its NAME in the scene tree (a rebuild under the same name overwrites the entry). No effect outside collection or if name is nil.

name.desc: Name of the object in the scene.

recordParts.desc: Records the geometry of ONE part of a mesh merged by structural category (bridge.deck, tunnel.floor, tunnel.shell). Additive: values add up. It is a breakdown of the mesh totals, not a duplicate.

report.desc: Aggregates everything and logs the summary, then ends the collection window. Without an active collection, logs '[mesh] no active mesh-stats session' and returns.
